title: Increased prices of groceries
body:
O.P.
I just noticed how stingy Uncle Toby's have gotten with the cheese dip in Le Snacks!! Over time they have shaped the plastic that holds the cheese into a compact area that is conveniently rounded small at the bottom to reduce the volume of dip! Furthermore, several months ago I was making myself toast in the morning, I opened the loaf of bread and pulled out a slice – I was absolutely astounded at the size of the piece of bread I held in my hand – its was so small! Ever since I noticed this phenomenon, I have noted that it was not a once off – our bread is shrinking and we are getting less for our money! Am I alone in my observations? Has anyone noticed this in other food products?

---- replies ----
[User #1032166187 postsWinusFree BurmaWhirlpool Forums Addict] UZ3R writes... we are getting less for our money! Often referred to as inflation . Has anyone noticed this in other food products? Whenever there's a new packaging... it's usually got a lesser volume for the same price. It's a well known trick.
[User #20225016729 postssnowantWhirlpool Forums Addict] I remember when Mars Bars shrank. They used to be wrapped up like a gift, with a little seal on the join. Then they moved to the current crimped-end packaging, and shrank the bars as they did it. Remember when Magnums first came out? They were huge! then as they upped the price, the downed the size.
[User #1032166187 postsWinusFree BurmaWhirlpool Forums Addict] Another trick that's often used is to "upsize" packaging. For instance, where you use to get a 250 gram jar of peanutbutter... they've now released a bigger jar... say 400 gram! At the same time, the 250 gram jar will be downsized to 200 gram... and will cost the same.
[User #475006530 postsXVIII.IV.MMIVClowns to left jokers to rightWhirlpool Forums Addict] UZ3R writes... Am I alone in my observations? Has anyone noticed this in other food products? The usual tactic is to reduce the size of the package contents and leave the pricing points untouched. I noticed this with potato crisps which seem to have a ubiquitous pricing point of $1.99 and it used to be that for 250 gram sizes but they have reduced the contents to 200 grams and leave the pricing point untouched and of course the goal of which is to dupe stupid end user customers and make more profit. This type of trick is as old as leaving your finger on the scale or injecting fresh meat and seafood with water and ice etc so that you end up paying $25 for (some quantity) of water. I guess they (the mfgrs and retailers) just seem to know the customers are really stupid.
[User #947523640 postsNot MeWhirlpool Forums Addict] UZ3R writes... Am I alone in my observations? Has anyone noticed this in other food products? No, this is common practice. This is why the big supermarkets are so against displaying unit pricing - it makes this kind of deception extremely obvious.

It'll probably go a bit further then to complete the cycle, there'll be a "New! Larger Size!" promotion with a matching larger price and they start again.
